LEARNING RARE LIFETIMES FROM LOCAL CLOCKS
Finite-error computation for driven Markov systems
Research developed 1 November 2026 (Australia/Brisbane)

Scope and status
===============
This is a self-contained mathematical construction and reproducible synthetic
calculation. It is not an experimentally validated device, an algorithm for
arbitrary unknown dynamics, or an established historical-priority claim.
Independent mathematical reconstructions and exact finite checks are included.
The positive result uses established Markov potential theory, sector estimates,
Poisson clocks and Monte Carlo. The proposed addition is the complete chain from
acquired local rate uncertainty, through uniform rare-target stability, to a
finite-error short-excursion receiver and later decisions.

Prior Astra research is bound to repository harjassand/astra-research-knowledge,
revision 51ce47ce39f976517d60e2f87bbe280b651f6056. Its 00_START_HERE.txt was the
first corpus file read. The decisive inherited obstruction is N1213's failure
of replacing a singleton return identity by a coarse-target indicator. The new
proof below is independent of any unavailable attachment from that record.
Source paths, conditions, comparisons and useful alternative failures are in
SOURCES_AND_COMPARISONS.txt and the independent notes in this package.

1. Intended consequence and exact contract
=========================================
Question: Can finite, ordinary-state calibration support reliable later
prediction of rare first-passage times in a driven stochastic system, without
waiting for those passages, preserving its entire long trajectory, or assuming
a precomputed committor? We construct such a service for the following class.

The source has a finite state space Omega and known executable maps P_a. Each
P_a is a permutation preserving the same known probability pi; uniform pi is
the principal explicit implementation. Every cycle of every P_a has length at
most ell >= 2. Independent Poisson clocks of unknown positive rates lambda_a
apply these maps. A clock mark remains observable even if its map fixes the
current state. This last requirement is an observation resource, not a
consequence of observing state changes.

On functions, with row-generator convention,
   Q f(x) = sum_a lambda_a [ f(P_a x) - f(x) ],    L = -Q.

RARE COARSE-TARGET LIFETIMES WITH AN ACQUIRED STATIONARY LAW
Root construction, synthesis, and executable contract
1 November 2026, Australia/Brisbane

What was strengthened
======================
MAIN_PROOF.txt first supplied the common stationary law and the target mass
and conditional sampler. The extension here earns those computational inputs
from local calibration for a restricted interacting model. It does not infer
an arbitrary physical mechanism. The pinned Astra N1213 acquisition ingredient
already learns local heatbath probabilities and compatible Ising weights;
this work credits and reuses that ingredient. The extension adds driven local
cycles, coarse targets, the joint weights/flows sensitivity proof, and the
screened mean and lifetime receiver. Standard inverse-Ising identification,
transfer matrices, Dobrushin coupling and potential theory remain its machinery.

An equally informed conventional method can adopt all these constructions.
No new universal feasibility class, strongest-method speed superiority or
historical priority has been established by this work.

1. A useful general sensitivity theorem
=======================================
Let L=-Q be a finite irreducible generator with positive unnormalized invariant
weights w. Write D=diag(w)L. The directed flows w(x)q_xy are balanced, so D has
zero row and column sums. Decompose this flow into positive directed cycle
coefficients c_j on a specified common cycle architecture. A cycle has length
at most ell. Its ordinary bilinear form B_j and energy E_j obey
   |B_j(f,h)| <= K sqrt(E_j(f) E_j(h)),   K=csc(pi/ell).
This follows from the Fourier modes of a cycle. Two- and three-cycles have
K=2/sqrt(3)<=7/6. This concerns STATIONARY-FLOW cycles; state-dependent accepted
moves need not themselves be permutation kernels.

Let the fitted model have weights what and coefficients chat_j, satisfying
   exp(-u) w <= what <= exp(u) w pointwise,
   exp(-v) c_j <= chat_j <= exp(v) c_j for every cycle.
For any nonempty proper target A, let M and Mhat be mean hitting times from
the respective stationary laws conditioned on B=A^c.

THEOREM 4 (weights and circulation).
   exp(-3u)/F(v,K) <= Mhat/M <= exp(3u) F(v,K),
   F(v,K)=exp(2 asinh(K sinh(v/2))) <= exp(Kv).              (G1)
Thus
   |log(Mhat/M)| <= 3u+Kv.                               (G2)

RESULTS, NECESSARY CONDITIONS AND USEFUL FAILURES

Authoritative retained outputs
===============================
main/qualified_intervals.json contains the final64-bit source mean intervals.
main/deadline_results.json contains its true conditional deadline intervals.
gibbs/gibbs_results.json contains the80-bit acquired model and final intervals.
gibbs/gibbs_deadline_results.json contains its true deadline intervals.
Paths above are relative to the research package root. The earlier floating
diagnostic intervals in main/large_results.json are superseded for final
reporting by the exact outward qualifications. Their samples are the same.

The64-bit mean source factor is conservatively300/293; the80-bit factor is5/4.
Both use a finite screening factor21/20. The reported confidence includes the
common calibration event and all finitely executed target simulation events.
There is no extra statistical charge for subsequently selecting a deadline.

Small-system ordinary benchmark
================================
The root directly solved killed Poisson systems on19 finite cases. This is
the correct ordinary method at those sizes and was not declared inferior.
One64-state fast-recrossing fixture has true mean0.6989965392201121. A
flux-only shortcut gives0.10271460014673514, only0.1469457921 of the correct
answer. Its screened estimate0.6951598084179247 lies within the proved interval
[0.6877119731842238,0.7026883027819464]. This is a failure of discarding return
information, not of strong conventional potential theory.

Independent mathematical checks
================================
The included audits separately reconstruct the identities and bounds.
 -240 exact rational nonreversible screening checks and120 rate checks.
 -48 additional exact rational capacity checks, including nonuniform pi.
 -336 exact rational target comparisons across12 models with changed
  stationary weights and changed2/3-cycle coefficients.
 -72 exact rational complex-resolvent checks and48 characteristic-function
  checks, plus12 phase-type CDF fixtures.
 -1120 additional complex-frequency checks and1200 CDF grid checks across
  eight reversible/nonreversible fixtures.
 -72 floating random cycle-family comparisons and two exact local Gibbs
  constructions, including stationary-flow and conditional-sampling checks.
These are different finite checks, not a proof by exhaustive enumeration.
